subject: Capacity tie-out: HyperNova deal runway & weekly commitments
content:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@hypernova.com>, HyperNova Procurement <procurement@hypernova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity tie-out: HyperNova deal runway & weekly commitments

Team / Rajiv —

Following up from last week's call: HyperNova is targeting a Q1 2027 GA with a phased rollout. I’ve attached the forecast they shared and a draft commit schedule. We need a clear capacity tie-out for the upcoming weekly fleet planning meeting (today, 3pm PT):

- HyperNova forecast (attached): 1500 peak concurrent tokens/day in Jan, ramping to 4200/day by Mar (consolidated into 24/7 GPU-hours equivalent).
- Ask: Can we commit to a monthly reserved vGPU pool for the pilot (Jan-Feb) with burst capacity for ramp?
- Required decision points for the meeting: commit size (monthly vGPU equivalents), SLA target for p95 latency, burst policy (credits or short-term instances), and pricing cadence.

Attachments: hypernova_forecast_q4_q1.csv; proposed_commit_schedule.pdf

I’ve looped in Laura (capacity), Karthik (capacity planning), Ben (infra burst/op), and Naomi (finance). Rajiv / procurement — please confirm your earliest PO timeframe; Naomi flagged that we need a signed PO by 12/15 to guarantee Q1 reserved pricing.

Proposed quick agenda for 3pm:
1) Confirm commit numbers Jan–Mar (Laura/Karthik)
2) Validate infra availability + burst implementation (Ben)
3) Finance ask / PO timeline (Naomi + Rajiv)
4) Next steps & cadence

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@hypernova.com>, HyperNova Procurement <procurement@hypernova.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity tie-out: HyperNova deal runway & weekly commitments

Monica / all —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick read of the attached forecast:
- If we map tokens/day into continuous vGPU-hours using the HyperNova workload profile, the conservative monthly reserved ask for Jan should be ~24 vGPU-hours/day (approx 72 vGPU-month) to meet p95 latency targets.
- Ramp to Mar looks like ~70 vGPU-hours/day (peak sustained periods) which we can accommodate with a mix of Reserved + Burst (GPU credit pool).

Risks / notes:
- Our current reserved pool for the region has ~15% headroom for Jan; to get to the conservative commit we’ll need to reassign ~40 vGPU-month from lower-priority trial customers or enable burst credits.
- If HyperNova requires a hard SLA for p95 <120ms, we should push for a larger reserved commit in the contract (or a higher price tier) to avoid throttling under load.

Action items for 3pm:
- I’ll bring a runway heatmap showing trade-offs (reserved vs burst) and a recommended commit schedule.
- Karthik, can you model a 20% safety margin scenario?

—Laura
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

> On Sat, Dec 5, 2026 at 08:12 AM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Team / Rajiv —
> > 
> > Following up from last week's call: HyperNova is targeting a Q1 2027 GA with a phased rollout...

---

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@hypernova.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: HyperNova Procurement <procurement@hypernova.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity tie-out: HyperNova deal runway & weekly commitments

Monica / Laura —

Thanks for the breakdown. A couple of notes from my side:
- Cost sensitivity: Our procurement committee will likely ask for a stepped pricing schedule tied to usage; full upfront commits are a stretch unless we get a pilot discount.
- PO timing: Procurement is targeting 12/20 for an initial PO (pilot) with the remainder by end of January post-pilot. Can Naomi confirm whether that PO timeline still allows the reserved pricing band?
- Trial ask: Would Redwood consider a 60-day pilot with a capped burst allowance before a full commit? That helps us validate performance and justify budget internally.

Attached: hypernova_po_draft.docx (draft PO with target milestones).

Regards,
Rajiv Menon
VP Product | HyperNova
rajiv@hypernova.com

---

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@hypernova.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 14:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity tie-out: HyperNova deal runway & weekly commitments

All —

I pulled a quick infra check: for the US-west region we can support the pilot profile with a combination of 48 reserved vGPU-month equivalents plus a burst pool sized at ~20% of projected peak. Implementation notes:
- Burst will be routed via short-lived spot-backed instances with pre-warmed kernels to reduce cold-start latency; that meets typical p95 SLAs if the burst is <30% of total traffic.
- We will need a 72-hour lead to reassign reserved capacity from trials (Laura / Karthik to flag donors).
- Monitoring: add a per-route cost/latency dashboard widget for HyperNova.

I’ll present the infra playbook at 3pm.

—Ben Carter
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@hypernova.com>, HyperNova Procurement <procurement@hypernova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity tie-out: HyperNova deal runway & weekly commitments

Rajiv / Monica —

Confirmed: per our pricing matrix, an initial PO by 12/15 at the pilot tier secures the pilot pricing; however to lock the full reserved discount band for Jan–Mar we need either:
1) Signed master and PO for minimum Jan reserved units by 12/20, or
2) A signed PO for the pilot by 12/15 plus a committed conversion timeline to reserved units by 1/15.

If procurement can do the 12/20 pilot PO, we can flip the commit with a consumption milestone. We can also include a 60-day pilot concession on burst credits (as requested) and convert credits to dollars on conversion.

Next steps: Monica — if you can confirm which procurement commitment HyperNova will accept, I’ll draft the invoice milestones and the contract addendum.

—Naomi Feldman
Finance Manager, Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

---

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@hypernova.com>, HyperNova Procurement <procurement@hypernova.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity tie-out: HyperNova deal runway & weekly commitments

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Quick recap / agreed next steps:
1) HyperNova to issue pilot PO by 12/20 (Rajiv) — Naomi to confirm pilot pricing terms and invoice milestones.
2) Redwood to reserve a pilot pool (target 48 vGPU-month equiv) and enable a burst pool (~20% of projected peak) for 60 days (Ben/Laura).
3) Karthik to run the 20% safety-margin model and circulate before 12/10.
4) Follow-up meeting scheduled: Monday 12/13, 10am PT (calendar invite sent).

I’ll attach the final commit schedule after the 12/13 checkpoint and keep the deal in the weekly fleet planning doc for this quarter.

Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
